title: Mother of the Church
hook: a title given by Paul VI at the Second Vatican Council, now a memorial on the Monday after Pentecost

segments.voice: Yesterday, Mary who stood at the cross, and comfort received and handed on. Your line was comfort of the afflicted. Did you take your shift? Day one thousand three hundred thirty-four.

"Woman, behold thy son." Those are words from the cross, in John's Gospel. Jesus is dying, and below him stand two people: his mother, and the disciple the Gospel calls the one whom he loved. He speaks to her first, then turns to the disciple: "Behold thy mother." And John adds a line that is easy to read past: "And from that hour, the disciple took her to his own." With a few words, at the worst hour, a family is made. A mother is given a son who isn't hers by birth. A friend is given a mother. Catholics hear that sentence as reaching much further than one house. Today's word is the name they give to where it reaches.
screen: `WOMAN, BEHOLD THY SON.` → `BEHOLD THY MOTHER.` → `A FAMILY MADE AT THE CROSS.`

segments.voice: Start with the disciple. John's Gospel never gives him a name in that scene. Catholics read that as an open door: the beloved disciple stands for every disciple, so behold thy mother is spoken to each of them. Some Christians read the scene more simply, as a dying son making sure his mother is looked after. Catholics hold that reading too, and hear more in it. Next, the upper room. In the Acts of the Apostles, after Jesus is taken up, his friends gather and pray together, with one mind, with the women and with Mary, the mother of Jesus. Then comes Pentecost, the coming of the Holy Spirit, a day sometimes called the Church's birthday. So Mary is there at the birth of Jesus, and in the room when the Church is born. Then the title. During the Second Vatican Council, Pope Paul the Sixth gave Mary the name Mother of the Church, and the Catechism puts it plainly in one line: Mother of Christ, Mother of the Church. The Council's teaching on Mary holds two things together. She is a member of the Church, one of the family, a believer like the rest. And she mothers it. Inside the family and caring for it, both at once. Finally, the calendar. Pope Francis made the title a memorial, and set it on the Monday after Pentecost. Pentecost is Sunday. On Monday, the Church remembers its mother. On an ordinary day that turns the Church from an institution into something more like a crowded kitchen table: a lot of people who didn't choose each other, handed to one another, with a mother keeping an eye on all of them.
screen: `THE DISCIPLE STANDS FOR EVERY DISCIPLE.` · `IN THE ROOM WHEN THE CHURCH IS BORN.` · `A MEMBER, AND A MOTHER.` · `THE MONDAY AFTER PENTECOST.` · then, large: `BEHOLD THY MOTHER.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: pray for the Church. Settle, and breathe. Bring the Church to mind not as a building, but as a table full of people. Start close: one parish you know, or one Catholic you know. Then widen it, one breath at a time. People who serve there. People who are tired of it. People who were hurt by it. People who walked away. People somewhere far off, gathering this week in places where it costs them. Let them all be at one table. If you pray, you can use the litany's line, Mother of the Church, pray for us, and leave them with her. If you don't, simply hold that crowded table, and wish it well. The bell holds the time.
Mother of the Church. Mary's title from the Second Vatican Council, kept on the Monday after Pentecost: a member of the family, and the one who mothers it. Today's word.
Your line: mother of the church. Today, treat one person you didn't choose as someone you were handed: a coworker, a neighbor, someone in the pew. Day one thousand three hundred thirty-four.

howItsDone: Catholics keep the memorial of the Blessed Virgin Mary, Mother of the Church, on the Monday after Pentecost, and the Litany of Loreto includes the invocation "Mother of the Church, pray for us."

original.note: Latin: Mother of the Church, the title Paul VI gave Mary.

trapdoor: what you thought: a grand title that sets Mary above everyone.
what it means: a member of the Church and its mother at once, from the cross (behold thy mother) to the upper room at Pentecost.
what a scholar hears: Paul VI's title from the Second Vatican Council, the Catechism's 'Mother of Christ, Mother of the Church' (CCC 963), and a memorial set on the Monday after Pentecost.

notes: The index hook names the years (Paul VI's title of 1964; a feast since 2018). Per the claims rule the voice states no year; the script hook field is reworded without dates. The index hook is unchanged; confirm the reworded script hook is acceptable.

Confirm Douay-Rheims (Challoner) wording of John 19:26–27 (19:26 "...he saith to his mother: Woman, behold thy son." 19:27 "After that, he saith to the disciple: Behold thy mother. And from that hour, the disciple took her to his own."), quoted in parts.
'The day the Church counts as its birth' for Pentecost: confirm phrasing (CCC 1076 speaks of the Church being made manifest at Pentecost).
Lumen Gentium 53 calls Mary a preeminent and wholly unique member of the Church; paraphrased as 'a member of the Church... and she mothers it'. Confirm.
'Mother of the Church, pray for us' as an invocation of the Litany of Loreto: added under John Paul II; confirm before shipping.

Reading the beloved disciple as standing for every disciple is presented as a Catholic reading; the simpler reading attributed to 'some Christians' and said to be held by Catholics too. Confirm fairness.
